The failed refresh (content_changed bedrock-models, extractor bedrock-catalog-v54) reported 155 models, 22319 rate facts and 419 raw facts, and the assembled provider partition exceeded providerPricingBytes (134217728). Replaying the current first-party source (sha256 c3600ae5..., changed_since_refresh, 45925744 body bytes) through the real parseSource with the reviewed manifest yields the same 155 models and 22319 rate facts with zero contract findings, so the parser accepts the current source and the failure is not a parse rejection. Measuring the committed retained partition with the validation byte semantics gives 130298033 bytes against the 134217728 limit, only 3919695 bytes of headroom, so the reviewed budget was already nearly saturated before this source change. Investigating the alternative explanation of avoidable compaction bloat found no same-offer variant groups with identical contract and price (0 groups), and the 16792035 duplicate observation bytes are state-versus-rate and per-variant evidence rather than removable duplication; equal-price variants differ in charge binding or selector mappings and correctly remain distinct. The remaining repair is therefore to raise the operator-reviewed providerPricingBytes/providerApplicabilityBytes budget (and its documented rationale and paired-limit invariant in tests/pricing-validation.test.ts), which is a capacity contract change outside automatic publication. No code change is submitted so that retry attempts stay genuine rather than raising a reviewed budget without operator review.
